cards.explanation: The answer is what must happen after these things. The voice says, “Come up here, and I will show you what must happen after these things.” So John, the one seeing all this, isn't getting a history lesson. He's getting a look at what's ahead.

The answer is rumblings and peals of thunder. Lightning gets the headlines, friends, but the verse gives the whole show: “From the throne came flashes of lightning, rumblings, and peals of thunder.” Flashes for the eyes, rumblings and peals for the ears. I'd be holding my mustache over my ears about now.

The answer is as clear as crystal. John sees “…something like a sea of glass, as clear as crystal.” Notice he says something like. He's reaching for words to describe what he sees. I've never gotten my oven door that clear.

The answer is False. The creatures say “…who was and is and is to come!” So yes, He was, but He also is, and He is to come. Past, present and future, friends, and they never stop saying it day and night. I lose my breath after one sneeze.

The answer is True. Whenever the living creatures give glory, honor and thanks to the One on the throne, the twenty-four elders fall down before Him. Then they worship Him who lives forever and ever. Notice the word whenever, bakers. It happens every time, not just once.

The answer is that they cast their crowns before the throne. The elders “…cast their crowns before the throne…” while they worship. Those are golden crowns going down in front of the throne. I'd have trouble letting go of my hat, friends, and mine is only cloth.

The answer is created. The elders say, “Worthy are You, our Lord and God, to receive glory and honor and power, for You created all things…” They say He's worthy because He created everything. Their praise starts with who made it all.

The answer is no one anywhere. The text says “…no one in heaven or on earth or under the earth was able to open the scroll or look inside it.” That covers heaven, earth and under the earth, friends. The answer to the angel's question is a long, quiet nobody.

The answer is True. John says, “And I began to weep bitterly, because no one was found worthy to open the scroll or look inside it.” John is the one writing this down, and he tells us about his own tears. He doesn't hide it.

The answer is Judah. The elder says, “Behold, the Lion of the tribe of Judah, the Root of David, has triumphed to open the scroll and its seven seals.” John was crying over a closed scroll, and the elder says someone has triumphed to open it. That's one big turn in a single verse, friends.

The answer is a Lamb who appeared slain. John writes, “Then I saw a Lamb who appeared to have been slain, standing in the center of the throne…” The elder had just said Lion, and John looks and sees a Lamb. Standing, bakers, though He appeared slain.
The answer is False. The verse says, “And He came and took the scroll from the right hand of the One seated on the throne.” The Lamb comes and takes the scroll Himself. Nobody brings it to Him.

The answer is prayers. John says they're holding “…golden bowls full of incense, which are the prayers of the saints.” So the incense in those bowls stands for the prayers of the saints. Nothing about those prayers is thrown away here, friends.

The answer is that He was slain and purchased people for God. They sing, “Worthy are You to take the scroll and open its seals, because You were slain, and by Your blood You purchased for God…” The song gives what He did as the reason He's worthy. The Lamb who was slain is the One who takes the scroll.

The answer is every tribe and tongue and nation. The song says He purchased people “…from every tribe and tongue and people and nation.” That's a wide circle, friends. Every tribe, every tongue, every people and every nation.

The answer is False. John says he heard “…every creature in heaven and on earth and under the earth and in the sea, and all that is in them…” So it isn't only heaven, bakers. Every creature joins the praise to Him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb.
